mainEntity.name: When is it a good time to work together?

acceptedAnswer.text: When your robots work in pilots but releases, customer-site deployments, or field incidents are becoming harder to manage. The assessment is a starting point for teams preparing to expand a fleet or improve an existing deployment workflow.

mainEntity.name: Do you implement changes or only advise?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both are possible. An assessment produces findings and an implementation roadmap. A separately scoped implementation engagement can cover release pipelines, OTA workflows, observability, and team handover. Fractional leadership is an option for ongoing technical direction.

mainEntity.name: Can you work with our existing team and infrastructure?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The starting point is your current robot platform, release process, and team. My experience covers ROS and ROS 2, on-premise, hybrid, and cloud-connected environments. We agree the access and engineering involvement needed for the scope before starting.

mainEntity.name: How are scope, timing, and fees agreed?

acceptedAnswer.text: Start with a LinkedIn message describing your fleet, deployment bottleneck, and next milestone. We discuss fit, then agree deliverables, responsibilities, timing, and fees before work begins. Implementation and ongoing support are scoped explicitly.

mainEntity.name: How does this relate to Robotair?

acceptedAnswer.text: I founded Robotair, a robotics DevOps infrastructure layer for packaging, OTA updates, and monitoring. This page is an invitation to discuss working with me on your deployment challenges. If your inquiry is about Robotair specifically, mention that in your message so we can clarify the appropriate scope.
